summary: Across 21 Cedar Commons HOA screens, the same five-row block — Property / Record / History / Owner inbox / Change option — is rendered verbatim on at least 12 screens, and its body text is disjunctive placeholder copy rather than the record actually on screen (e.g. 'Community Rules, Room A reservation, dues receipt, or architectural case' appears on the dues payment, fence request, committee decision, and room reservation screens alike). Most descriptive text is written as capability spec rather than product copy — sentences ending in 'are visible', 'remain visible', 'match the state' — so a homeowner reading these screens learns what the app can display, not what their own reservation, dues bill, or fence request says. Several screens also show cross-workflow bleed: the facility-reservation action sheet asks the user to 'Choose attendance … Going, Maybe, or Not going' for a clubhouse room booking, the dues-payment start screen surfaces a 'Facility reservation a…' card, and the member-document start screen surfaces an 'HOA export' card. Only the owner-notification trio carries genuinely specific copy ('Your slate gray fence repaint is approved if trim remains cedar and work starts within 30 days', 'Send today at 4:15 PM'), which proves the bar the other five workflows fall short of; the review fails.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Across this community's workflows, is it always clear what workflow and what state (start/in-progress/complete) the user is looking at?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Partially. The action and complete states are usually legible — action sheets carry a specific modal title ('Clubhouse Room A reservation', 'Fence color request', 'Quarterly HOA dues', 'HOA records export', 'Community Rules document', 'Send owner notice'), and complete screens carry an explicit terminal banner ('HOA record saved', 'Request outcome saved', 'Owner notified', 'Member result'). The start states are much weaker: five of seven open mid-scroll under the generic 'Cedar Commons HOA' app bar with no workflow title in view, so the facility-reservation start screen leads with a clipped 'Cedar Commons / Receipt/audit' chip row and a 'Response choices' card, and the architectural-request start screen leads with a half-cut line reading 'Commons HOA; sender is the HOA board.' Worse, the workflow identity on several start screens contradicts the row: the dues-payment start screen's only titled card is 'Facility reservation a…', and the member-document start screen's only titled card is 'HOA export'. A 'Waiting' pill appears on the export, architectural-request, and member-document starts without saying what is being waited on.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the displayed text read as real product copy describing actual Cedar Commons HOA content, or as generic template/spec filler?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Mostly spec filler. The recurring 'Record' row lists four unrelated record types joined by 'or' — 'Community Rules, Room A reservation, dues receipt, or architectural case' — on screens where exactly one of those is the subject, which is template text that was never resolved to the instance. The same is true of 'Change option: Cancel reservation, request changes, retry payment, or reopen where policy allows', shown identically on a document view and a payment. Section bodies are written from the capability spec's point of view: 'Payer, amount, privacy choice, entitlement, receipt destination, and retry/refund options are visible', 'Labeled fields, privacy indicators, attachments, assignee, and status are visible', 'Scope, redaction, checksum, destination, transfer status, rollback, and audit evidence are visible'. These describe the UI instead of showing the data — the dues screens never show a dollar amount, the export screens never show a file size or checksum value, and the reservation screens never show a date or time slot. The owner-notification and architectural-request screens are the exceptions with real specifics: 'Lot 42 fence repaint, slate gray, decision due Friday' and 'Your slate gray fence repaint is approved if trim remains cedar and work starts within 30 days.'

By contrast the owner-notification screens show 'Send today at 4:15 PM to owner inbox and email receipt.' — a concrete, instance-level fact

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Do the screens avoid repeated generic card shells and thin/empty content where real content is expected?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No. The identical five-row icon list (house/Property, page/Record, clock/History, tray/Owner inbox, undo/Change option) is the dominant visual unit on at least twelve of the twenty-one screens, appearing as 'Event details', 'Export steps', 'Decision queue', 'Payment summary', 'Submitted details', and 'Submitted request' — six different headings over one identical body. Two screens duplicate the block within a single scroll: the facility-reservation action sheet shows 'Event details / Property / Lot 42, homeowner Avery Brooks…' at the top and again inside 'Choose attendance' at the bottom, and the owner-notification action sheet shows 'Sender and recipient / Message body' twice, once under 'Notice preview' and again under 'Delivery actions'. The export-evidence and member-document start screens both end in roughly 500px of empty dark canvas below a collapsed 'Local package details' row. Chip rows ('Cedar Commons', 'Receipt/audit', 'Documents', 'Availability', 'Outcome history') repeat verbatim across workflows and are visually indistinguishable from each other.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are the available actions clear, and is it clear why disabled or minimized affordances are in that state?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Uneven. Primary verbs are strong where present — 'Reserve and pay', 'Pay and save receipt', 'Approve request', 'Generate export', 'Open document', 'Submit request' all say what will happen. But the recurring dark card carries a 'Minimized' chip with a target-reticle icon alongside both 'Tap for expanded view' and 'Expand' — three affordances that appear to do the same thing, and 'Minimized' is a state label styled as a button with no explanation of why the card is minimized. The 'Waiting' pill on three start screens names no blocking condition. On the member-document start screen the action slot reads 'Read only' with an eye icon — presented as a button but actually a permission state, with nothing saying why editing is unavailable. The 'Change details' and 'Request changes' buttons are rendered in a low-contrast translucent style over the blue card that reads closer to disabled than enabled.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the content shown on each screen make sense for the workflow being demonstrated?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Not consistently. The clearest defect is the facility-reservation action sheet titled 'Clubhouse Room A reservation' whose main interactive card is 'Choose attendance — Event date, capacity, location, host note, and reminders are visible before choosing Going, Maybe, or Not going', with an 'Attendance options: Going, Maybe, Not going, and Change response remain available while the event is open' row. That is an RSVP-to-an-event model applied to booking a room; a homeowner reserving Room A does not RSVP to their own booking. Beyond that, the dues-payment start screen's foreground card is a facility-reservation card, the member-document start screen's foreground card is an HOA export card, the facility-reservation start screen's foreground card is 'Architectural request' with a 'Submit request' button, and the committee-decision start screen's foreground card is 'Member-visible docu…' with 'Waiting for the member form to be submitted.' In each case the state being demonstrated belongs to a different workflow than the row claims.

findings.title: 'Community Rules, Room A reservation, dues receipt, or architectural case' renders as the record identity on every workflow
findings.description: The 'Record' row prints a four-way 'or' list of every record type in the community rather than the record actually in context. It appears verbatim on the facility-reservation action and complete screens, the export action screen, the architectural-request start/action/complete screens, the dues-payment action and complete screens, and the committee-decision action and complete screens. On screens whose own title already names the record ('Fence color request', 'Quarterly HOA dues', 'Clubhouse Room A reservation'), the disjunction directly contradicts the header. The same pattern appears in 'Change option — Cancel reservation, request changes, retry payment, or reopen where policy allows', shown identically on a document view, a payment, and a decision queue.
findings.requiredFix: Bind the Record and Change-option rows to the instance in context so each screen names one record ('Clubhouse Room A booking, Sat Aug 15') and offers only the change actions that apply to that record's current state.

findings.title: Facility reservation action sheet asks the user to RSVP Going/Maybe/Not going to their own room booking
findings.description: The sheet titled 'Clubhouse Room A reservation' contains 'Choose attendance — Event date, capacity, location, host note, and reminders are visible before choosing Going, Maybe, or Not going', with a supporting row 'Attendance options: Going, Maybe, Not going, and Change response remain available while the event is open' and 'Member reminder — The saved response keeps calendar, reminder, and capacity status visible.' This is an events/RSVP interaction model rendered on a facility-booking workflow. A homeowner reserving a room selects a time slot and pays a fee; they do not respond to an invitation. The action state of this workflow therefore demonstrates the wrong interaction entirely.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the attendance card with reservation controls: date and time-slot selection, capacity/conflict check against existing bookings, deposit amount, and Confirm reservation / Change slot / Cancel actions.

findings.title: Start screens foreground a card from a different workflow than the row under test
findings.description: Four of seven start states put a card belonging to another workflow in the visual foreground: the dues-payment start screen's dominant card is 'Facility reservation a…' with a 'Reserve and pay' button; the member-document start screen's dominant card is 'HOA export' with a download icon and 'Read only'; the facility-reservation start screen's dominant card is 'Architectural request' with 'Submit request'; and the committee-decision start screen's dominant card is 'Member-visible docu…' reading 'Waiting for the member form to be submitted.' In the last case the borrowed card's waiting state also contradicts the actionable 'Approve request' button above it. A reviewer or homeowner landing on these screens would identify the wrong workflow.
findings.requiredFix: Scope each start screen's foreground card to its own workflow, and open the screen at the top so the workflow title is the first thing rendered rather than a mid-scroll fragment.

findings.title: Committee decision start offers 'Approve request' with no case, requester, or requested change on screen
findings.description: The committee-decision start screen presents a full-width 'Approve request' pill and a 'Request changes' button, but nothing in the viewport identifies what is being approved — no case title, no homeowner name, no requested change, no attachments, no deadline. The visible text is a clipped 'Homeowner sees receipt, decision, document,' fragment, the generic 'Change option' row, and 'Request queue — Approve, reject, request changes, comment, or reopen with a visible owner notification state.' Offering a consequential, owner-notifying approval action against an unnamed subject is the most serious actionability defect in this set.
findings.requiredFix: Render the case under review above the decision controls — case title, homeowner, lot, requested change, attachments, and applicable rule — and disable the approve action until a case is in context.

findings.title: Descriptive copy asserts that values 'are visible' while none are rendered
findings.description: Section bodies across the community are written as acceptance criteria rather than product copy, and in several cases the assertion is false as rendered. 'Payer, amount, privacy choice, entitlement, receipt destination, and retry/refund options are visible' appears on a dues checkout showing no amount. 'Scope, redaction, checksum, destination, transfer status, rollback, and audit evidence are visible' appears on an export sheet showing no scope, checksum, or destination. 'Labeled fields, privacy indicators, attachments, assignee, and status are visible' appears on a request sheet with no fields, attachments, or assignee. The result is that the dues workflow never shows a dollar figure, the export workflow never shows a file, and the reservation workflow never shows a date or time.
findings.requiredFix: Replace every '… are visible' / '… remain visible' / '… match the state' sentence with the actual values: amounts, dates, file sizes, checksums, assignee names, and status chips rendered as data.

findings.title: One five-row block is reused under six different headings across twelve screens
findings.description: The Property / Record / History / Owner inbox / Change option list with identical icons and identical body text is rendered under the headings 'Event details', 'Export steps', 'Decision queue', 'Payment summary', 'Submitted details', and 'Submitted request'. Numbering it 1–5 on the export screen turns unrelated content into fake 'Export steps' whose step 5 reads 'Cancel reservation, request changes, retry payment, or reopen where policy allows.' The committee-decision action sheet is pixel-identical to the architectural-request action sheet below the header. Two screens duplicate the block within one scroll view (facility-reservation action, owner-notification action). The effect is that six workflows look like one workflow with six titles.
findings.requiredFix: Give each workflow a purpose-built body — booking slots for reservations, line items for dues, a record picker for exports, vote and conditions for committee decisions — and remove the duplicate render of the identity block within a single scroll view.

findings.title: Completion screens confirm that a record was saved without stating what happened
findings.description: Four completions share the banner body 'The homeowner record now shows owner, amount or decision, status history, and member next steps.' The reservation completion never states the booked date or fee; the dues completion never states the amount paid or the method; the export completion says 'HOA record saved' rather than confirming a file was produced, and never names a filename, size, or destination; the committee-decision completion never says whether the request was approved, rejected, or conditioned. 'amount or decision' is itself an unresolved disjunction. Several of these banners are additionally clipped by the bottom nav mid-sentence.
findings.requiredFix: Write outcome-specific confirmations that lead with the result and its key facts — amount paid and method, room/date booked with confirmation number, file generated with size and destination, decision reached with conditions — rather than a shared 'record saved' sentence.

findings.title: Content and primary controls are severed horizontally by the persistent bottom nav
findings.description: Multiple screens render content under the Home/Board/Documents/Payments bar instead of padding above it: 'Edit notice' on the owner-notification start is cut in half; 'Download PDF' on the member-document complete is clipped; 'Change option' on the export complete is cut mid-glyph; the 'Request outcome saved' banners on both the architectural-request and committee-decision completions lose their body text; the 'After delivery' card on the owner-notification complete is truncated to its heading; and the dues-payment start ends in an illegible partial card heading. The bottom nav's rightmost item ('Messages') is also cut off at the right screen edge on several screens.
findings.requiredFix: Add bottom-inset padding equal to the nav bar height to all scroll containers so no content or control renders beneath it, and make the nav bar's item set fit the viewport width.

findings.title: 'Minimized', 'Waiting', and 'Read only' render as buttons without explaining the state
findings.description: The recurring dark card shows a 'Minimized' chip with a target-reticle icon next to both 'Tap for expanded view' and a separate 'Expand' button — three overlapping affordances plus a state label styled identically to them. A 'Waiting' pill with a clock icon appears on the export-evidence, architectural-request, and member-document start screens with no adjacent text naming what is pending. On the member-document start screen 'Read only' with an eye icon occupies the primary action slot with no reason given for why the document cannot be edited or acknowledged there. Low-contrast translucent buttons ('Change details', 'Request changes', 'Open document' on blue cards) further blur the enabled/disabled distinction.
findings.requiredFix: Style state indicators distinctly from controls, give each pending state a subject ('Waiting on board review since Aug 4'), state why an item is read-only, collapse the three expand affordances to one, and raise disabled/enabled contrast so the two are distinguishable.

findings.title: Export and member-document start screens end in a large empty region
findings.description: Both the export-evidence start and member-document start screens place a collapsed 'Local package details' disclosure row roughly two-thirds down the screen and render nothing below it — approximately a third of a page of blank dark canvas above the bottom nav. This is exactly where the export's record list, file size, and destination, or the document's version history and acknowledgement status, would be expected. Combined with the truncated card bodies above ('Data package includes scope, protected fields, a…', 'You can read the current details without changing …'), these screens present less readable content than empty space.
findings.requiredFix: Fill the lower region with the substantive content these workflows own — record list with sizes for the export, version history and acknowledgement state for the document — and expand the truncated card bodies rather than ellipsising them.

findings.title: Owner-notice send sheet renders the full notice twice and exposes no send control
findings.description: On the 'Send owner notice' sheet, 'Sender and recipient — From Cedar Commons HOA Board to Avery Brooks, homeowner for Lot 42' and 'Message body — Your slate gray fence repaint is approved if trim remains cedar and work starts within 30 days' appear in full under 'Notice preview' and again verbatim under 'Delivery actions', with a third 'Delivery' row starting below the fold. Between the copies sit two spec sentences ('Sender, recipient or audience, timestamp, body, and delivery channel are visible', 'Reply, read/unread, archive, mute, block, draft, or resend actions match the message state'). No Send button appears anywhere in the viewport on the sheet whose title is 'Send owner notice'.
findings.requiredFix: Show the notice once, replace the capability sentences with the notice's actual channel and scheduled time as editable values, and surface Send now / Schedule / Save draft controls in the sheet.

findings.title: 'In-focus product surface' harness strip renders above product content
findings.description: The owner-notification start screen shows a dark strip directly beneath the app bar reading 'In-focus product surface' with a target-reticle icon and an 'Expand' link on the right. This is framing language about the capture itself rather than product UI; a homeowner would never see a label describing a surface as 'in-focus'. It occupies the position where the workflow title 'Owner decision notice' should sit — that heading instead appears well below the preview card, mid-scroll.
findings.requiredFix: Remove the in-focus/minimized harness chrome from the product surface and place the 'Owner decision notice' heading above the notice preview card.

findings.title: Secondary actions render at very low contrast against their backgrounds
findings.description: 'Download PDF' on the member-document action sheet is drawn in a dark teal on the dark navy panel, at a contrast level where it reads as decorative text rather than a control, and it sits at the clipped viewport edge. The same low-contrast treatment affects translucent white-on-blue buttons throughout: 'Change details' on the dues and facility-reservation starts, 'Reserve and pay' and 'Pay and save receipt' pills, 'Open document' on the member-document start, and 'Save document' on the document screens all render as pale outlines over the blue card, visually closer to disabled than to available.
findings.requiredFix: Raise secondary-action contrast to meet accessible minimums against both the navy and blue card backgrounds, and reserve the translucent style exclusively for genuinely disabled controls.

findings.title: A bordered card containing only a spec sentence and 'Save document' has no heading
findings.description: On both member-document screens, a bordered card renders with no title at all — its entire content is the sentence 'Document access, version, download, save, share, and access-request options are visible.' followed by a 'Save document' button. Without a heading the card reads as an empty shell wrapped around a caption, and it sits directly above a separate card that is titled 'Document access' and covers overlapping ground ('Open, download, acknowledge, request access, or view version history'), so two adjacent cards describe the same capability set with only one of them labeled.
findings.requiredFix: Merge the unlabeled card into the titled 'Document access' section so save, download, share, and access-request controls appear once under one heading.
